gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 29?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 29 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data is unavailable or missing for the observation period, Weather Underground will be used as the secondary resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

**Official National Weather Service forecasts for August 31, 2026, in New York City consistently indicate a daytime high in the lower 80s°F (around 81–83°F), with partly sunny skies after morning clouds, light north-to-southeast winds, and only a 20% chance of showers.** This aligns closely with the market's leading bins (80–81°F at 29.5%, 78–79°F at 26.0%, and 82–83°F at 21.5%), reflecting trader consensus around these guidance values.

Key differentiating factors include the extent of morning cloud cover versus afternoon solar heating, subtle differences in low-level wind direction that modulate coastal marine influence or warm advection, and the precise timing or intensity of any scattered showers, which could briefly limit peak temperatures. Ensemble model spreads at this short lead time (roughly two days out) remain modest but allow for small adjustments in the exact maximum, particularly if a stronger ridge or drier air mass materializes. Late-August climatology for the region supports highs near 82°F as a baseline, so current guidance sits right at seasonal norms with limited deviation expected absent a major pattern shift. Updated model runs and NWS briefings in the next 24–48 hours will likely refine these probabilities further.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast consensus from multiple numerical weather prediction models places Munich’s maximum temperature on August 31 near 24–25 °C, driving the market’s heavy weighting toward those outcomes. Persistent westerly flow, increasing cloud cover, and a 40–80 % chance of showers or thunderstorms during the day are expected to limit solar heating and cap the afternoon peak, consistent with late-August climatology where the long-term average high is 22.4 °C. Recent model runs have shown little shift in this range, leaving only modest implied probability for 26 °C or higher under clearer, drier scenarios. Traders are therefore pricing in the narrow uncertainty band typical of a 24-hour forecast horizon.

Persistent westerly flow, increasing cloud cover, and a 40–80 % chance of showers or thunderstorms during the day are expected to limit solar heating and cap the afternoon peak, consistent with late-August climatology where the long-term average high is 22.4 °C. Recent model runs have shown little shift in this range, leaving only modest implied probability for 26 °C or higher under clearer, drier scenarios. Traders are therefore pricing in the narrow uncertainty band typical of a 24-hour forecast horizon.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 31 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and global models indicate a mostly cloudy Monday for Tokyo with easterly flow and a modest chance of afternoon showers or thunderstorms, limiting peak insolation and capping the daily maximum near 29–31 °C. Persistent marine air and high humidity further moderate temperatures by enhancing cloud cover and reducing daytime heating rates. Model consensus shows only modest spread around these values, with differences between 29 °C and 31 °C hinging on the exact timing of any breaks in the overcast and the strength of the sea-breeze circulation. Historical August normals near 30 °C provide context, yet the current pattern of post-frontal stabilization favors outcomes clustered in the upper 20s to low 30s rather than extremes. Updated model runs and JMA briefings tomorrow morning will refine the final observed maximum before market resolution.
